item.title: PRINCIPAL TO AGENCY: Uber restructures driver contracts outside of London to sidestep VAT hit from Rachel Reeves minicab tax reforms
item.description: Uber has rewritten its driver contracts across England and Wales outside London in a move that protects its exposure to the Government’s new VAT rules for private hire, just as the changes are about to come into force. Under updated terms issued to drivers from January 2026, Uber has restructured its role so that it acts as an agent rather than the supplier of transport services outside of London. This aims to shift the relationship so that drivers are treated as contracting directly with...

item.title: Chancellor Reeves shuts TOMS VAT loophole used by private hire firms like Uber as from today
item.description: Private hire vehicle operators in London will no longer be able to use the Tour Operators Margin Scheme to reduce the amount of VAT paid on passenger fares as from today, following a policy change first confirmed at Budget 2025. The measure, announced by the Chancellor, closes off a long criticised route that allowed a small number of large ride-hailing and minicab platforms to apply a specialist VAT regime intended for tour operators and holiday travel businesses. item.title: We’ve heard Uber’s autonomous vehicle roadmap, but what is Bolt’s 2026 plans?
item.description: Image credit: Bolt Bolt has outlined plans to begin large-scale deployment of autonomous vehicles in Europe from 2026, confirming a long-term ambition to host 100,000 driverless vehicles on its platform by 2035. item.title: New Year ride-hail surge pricing continues to ease, Obi data suggests
item.description: Ride-hailing price surges around New Year appear to be moderating, according to new analysis from US-based price aggregator Obi , which found that fare volatility during the holiday period has declined steadily since 2022. Data covering the eight-day period from Christmas Eve to New Year’s Day shows that the difference between high and low daily average prices across major US ride-hailing platforms has narrowed significantly. item.title: Private hire driver arrested on drink-driving suspicion after Merseyside minicab smashes into van
item.description: A private hire driver has been arrested on suspicion of drink driving following a collision involving a stationary van in Huyton, Merseyside Police confirmed. The incident was reported shortly after 9.05pm on Wednesday 31 December on Fincham Road, where a red Toyota Corolla operating as a private hire vehicle was involved in a collision with a parked van. item.title: London taxi marshals mark two years at Liverpool Street under women’s safety scheme
item.description: Taxi marshals operating at Liverpool Street Station have marked two years in place under the City of London-backed Our Safer City women’s safety initiative, as industry figures highlight sustained demand for supervised night-time taxi provision in the Square Mile. The milestone was marked this week by London Taxi PR presenting marshals with branded umbrellas linked to its Choose Taxi campaign. item.title: London Congestion Charge now applies to electric private hire vehicles
item.description: Electric private hire vehicles are now required to pay the London Congestion Charge after the expiry of the Cleaner Vehicle Discount, marking a significant cost change for drivers working in central London who must now cover the extra cost. As of Friday 2 January 2026, the 100 percent Cleaner Vehicle Discount has ceased. As a result, electric private hire vehicles (PHV) entering the Congestion Charge zone during operational hours are liable for the daily charge, bringing EV PHVs into line...

item.description: Image credit: Freenow by Lyft Freenow has outlined an expanded European growth strategy and confirmed preparations to introduce autonomous vehicles from 2026, as the company moves into its first full year under the ownership of Lyft following a landmark acquisition. item.title: BLACK CAB BOOST: Rachel Reeves says VAT rule change will allow London black cabs to ‘compete fairly on price from 2026’
item.description: Image credit: Simon Walker / HM Treasury The Chancellor has said changes to VAT rules announced at the Budget will allow London’s black taxi drivers to compete more fairly on price with large online minicab operators from 2026, after years of what the trade describes as distorted competition.
